title: Rotate Array
statement: Rotate `nums` to the right by `k` steps and return the rotated array. k may be larger than the length.
hints: k modulo n is the effective rotation.
The last k elements become the new prefix.
Three reversals do it in place: reverse the whole array, reverse the first k, reverse the rest.

approaches.name: Extra array
approaches.explanation: Write each element to (i + k) mod n.

approaches.name: Three reversals
approaches.explanation: In-place, no extra buffer beyond a few indices.

editorial: Reduce k modulo n. Reverse the entire array, then reverse the first k elements, then reverse the suffix. The first reversal puts the old suffix at the front in reverse. The next two reversals restore order inside each piece.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def rotate(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums)
    k %= n
    nums.reverse()
    nums[:k] = reversed(nums[:k])
    nums[k:] = reversed(nums[k:])
    return nums
